newsitem.title: UK: Celltech, Cortecs climb on drug hopes.
newsitem.headline: Celltech, Cortecs climb on drug hopes.

text.p: Shares in a clutch of UK biotech stocks were higher in late Wednesday morning trading on the back of growing optimism about products in late-stage development.

Slough-based Celltech Group Plc has climbed 9 percent since Tuesday morning. It added another 22-1/2 pence to rise to 580 pence late Wednesday morning, building on Tuesday's 25 pence gain. Analysts said a strong buy note from brokers Greig Middleton and a recommendation from a U.S. broker and fund manager had supported the stock.
Cortecs International Plc was another strong gainer, climbing 14-1/2 pence or 8 percent to 203 pence.
Cortecs announced its first European marketing partnership for Oral Calcitonin on Tuesday with Ferrer International SA of Spain. The company already has deals sealed in Japan and Israel.

Yamaichi International analyst Erling Refsum, who is a strong supporter of Cortecs, said the agreement "shows that the people who matter, i.e. the pharmaceutical companies, believe in oral calcitonin."
The bone-wasting disease osteoporosis is a serious problem for the growing ageing population and Cortecs' drug can be taken orally rather than as a nasal spray.
Other biotechs forging ahead on Wednesday included Stanford Rook Plc, up 17 1/2 pence at 517 1/2.

Late-stage trial results on Stanford Rook's tuberculosis drug are expected to be published in the spring. Analysts said the technology behind the drug has a vast range of other possible uses, including HIV, cancer and rheumatoid arthritis.

Scotia Holdings Plc was another riser, adding 7 1/2 pence to 727 1/2. Yamaichi's Refsum said there is starting to be a change in perception towards the company which is developing products based on fatty acids and currently has 30 drugs in development.
